## Measure details

-   Description: Ratio of population to primary care physicians.

-   Data Source: Area Health Resource File/American Medical Association

-   Data Download Link: <https://data.hrsa.gov/data/download>

-   Numerator: The number of primary care physicians in a county. Primary care physicians include practicing non-federal physicians (M.D.s and D.O.s) under age 75 specializing in general practice medicine, family medicine, internal medicine, and pediatrics. Physicians are counted at their mailing address.

-   Denominator: The total 2022 resident population of a county from the Vintage 2022 Census population estimates.

-   Data year: physician counts as of December 2022 (AHRF 2023-2024 release, Feb 2025 file); population 2022.

## Notes

**This is a draft.** It shows what the v004 script would look like if the methods changes in `R-Provider-Measures-Handoff.md` replace the current method. It writes no files. The official output is still produced by `v004_PCPs.R`.

Changes from the current method:

1.  **Two population cutoffs, 5,000 and 10,000** (was one cutoff of 2,000), for deciding how to treat counties with zero primary care physicians.
2.  **Zero physicians, population 5,000 or fewer:** shown as a real zero (`v004_rawvalue` = 0), status `none_reported`.
3.  **Zero physicians, population 5,001 to 10,000:** shown as a real zero, status `none_reported_caution`.
4.  **Zero physicians, population above 10,000:** value blank, status `none_reported_verify`.
5.  **Ratio for zero physicians:** always blank (population per physician is undefined at zero); the status column explains why. The same rule will apply to dentists, mental health and other primary care providers.
6.  **Small counts flagged:** counties with 1 to 4 physicians keep their value but get status `fewer_than_5` (less reliable). Counties with 5 or more are `reported`. Connecticut is `not_calculated`, and anything else is `no_data`.
7.  **National values computed from the data** instead of typed in.

Connecticut: this measure was not updated for Connecticut with the 2024-2025 release of the AHRF. The AHRF has data for the eight former CT counties, but there is no recent population data for those counties to use as a denominator. CHR&R also decided not to update CT data for any measures in the rolling 2025 updates because of the geography changes. CT counties and the CT state value are left blank and flagged `U`. CT physicians and population still count toward the national value.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(here)

#population cutoffs for zero-physician counties, and the small-count threshold
pop_cutoff_low  <- 5000
pop_cutoff_high <- 10000
small_count     <- 5
```

## Calculating the numerator - counties

```{r}
#official list of CHR&R counties (includes both the old CT counties and the new CT planning regions)
chrr_fips <- read_sas(here("inputs/county_fips_with_ct_old.sas7bdat"))

ahrf <- read_csv(here("raw_data/AHRF/ahrf2024_Feb2025.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(
    fipscode   = fips_st_cnty,
    statecode  = fips_st,
    countycode = fips_cnty,
    v004_numerator = phys_nf_prim_care_pc_exc_rsdt_22
  ) %>%
  #keep only CHR&R counties. This drops Puerto Rico, USVI and Guam, and six AK/VA counties that no
  #longer exist (02201, 02232, 02261, 02280, 51515, 51560); see the NOTE at the bottom of the AHRF
  #2023-2024 Technical Documentation and
  #https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/technical-documentation/county-changes.2010.html
  semi_join(chrr_fips, by = "fipscode")

#every CHR&R county should be in the AHRF
stopifnot(nrow(ahrf) == nrow(chrr_fips))
```

## Calculating the denominator - counties

```{r}
county_pop22 <- read_sas(here("inputs/vintage2022_with_ct_new.sas7bdat")) %>%
  filter(countycode != "000") %>%
  transmute(
    fipscode = paste0(statecode, countycode),
    v004_denominator = POPESTIMATE2022
  )
```

## Combining counties, states and the nation

The AHRF has physician counts for the old CT counties, and the population file has the new CT planning regions. Both are summed into the national value. CT is then blanked at the county and state level.

```{r}
counties <- ahrf %>%
  left_join(county_pop22, by = "fipscode")

#national value: sum of all counties (computed, no longer typed in)
national <- tibble(
  fipscode = "00000", statecode = "00", countycode = "000",
  v004_numerator   = sum(ahrf$v004_numerator, na.rm = TRUE),
  v004_denominator = sum(county_pop22$v004_denominator)
)

#state values: sum of counties in each state
states <- counties %>%
  group_by(statecode) %>%
  summarise(
    v004_numerator   = sum(v004_numerator, na.rm = TRUE),
    v004_denominator = sum(v004_denominator, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(countycode = "000", fipscode = paste0(statecode, countycode))

v004_base <- bind_rows(national, states, counties) %>%
  #CT not updated for this release: blank county and state values
  mutate(
    v004_numerator   = if_else(statecode == "09", NA_real_, v004_numerator),
    v004_denominator = if_else(statecode == "09", NA_real_, v004_denominator)
  ) %>%
  arrange(fipscode)
```

## Measure calculation

-   `v004_rawvalue` is physicians per person.
-   `v004_rawalternatevalue` is the ratio of population to physicians, which is how the measure is displayed on the website.

```{r}
v004 <- v004_base %>%
  mutate(
    v004_status = case_when(
      statecode == "09"                                         ~ "not_calculated", # CT
      v004_numerator == 0 & v004_denominator <= pop_cutoff_low  ~ "none_reported",
      v004_numerator == 0 & v004_denominator <= pop_cutoff_high ~ "none_reported_caution",
      v004_numerator == 0 & v004_denominator >  pop_cutoff_high ~ "none_reported_verify",
      v004_numerator >= 1 & v004_numerator < small_count        ~ "fewer_than_5",
      v004_numerator >= small_count                             ~ "reported",
      TRUE                                                      ~ "no_data"
    ),
    #rate: 0 for none_reported and none_reported_caution, blank for none_reported_verify
    v004_rawvalue = if_else(v004_status == "none_reported_verify", NA_real_,
                            v004_numerator / v004_denominator),
    #ratio: blank whenever there are 0 physicians (undefined)
    v004_rawalternatevalue = if_else(v004_numerator == 0, NA_real_,
                                     v004_denominator / v004_numerator),
    v004_cilow  = NA_real_,
    v004_cihigh = NA_real_,
    problem     = NA,
    v004_flag_ct = if_else(statecode == "09", "U", NA_character_)
  ) %>%
  select(fipscode, statecode, countycode,
         v004_numerator, v004_denominator, v004_rawvalue, v004_rawalternatevalue,
         v004_cilow, v004_cihigh, problem, v004_status, v004_flag_ct)
```

## Checks

### Counties by status

```{r}
v004 %>%
  filter(countycode != "000") %>%
  count(v004_status)
```

### Comparison with the current published values

The only expected differences from the current published file (`v004_r2026.csv`, read only) are counties that were blank and now show a real zero.

```{r}
published <- read_csv(here("measure_datasets/v004_r2026.csv"),
                      col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
  transmute(fipscode,
            numerator_pub = as.numeric(v004_numerator),
            denominator_pub = as.numeric(v004_denominator),
            rawvalue_pub = as.numeric(v004_rawvalue),
            ratio_pub = as.numeric(v004_rawalternatevalue))

same_value <- function(a, b) (is.na(a) & is.na(b)) | coalesce(abs(a - b) < 1e-9, FALSE)

comparison <- v004 %>%
  full_join(published, by = "fipscode") %>%
  mutate(
    change = case_when(
      !same_value(v004_numerator, numerator_pub) |
        !same_value(v004_denominator, denominator_pub)       ~ "inputs differ",
      is.na(rawvalue_pub) & !is.na(v004_rawvalue)          ~ "blank -> zero",
      !same_value(v004_rawvalue, rawvalue_pub) |
        !same_value(v004_rawalternatevalue, ratio_pub)       ~ "other difference",
      TRUE                                                 ~ "same"
    )
  )

comparison %>% count(change)

#nothing other than blank -> zero should differ
stopifnot(all(comparison$change %in% c("same", "blank -> zero")))
```
